why: Both analyses land on essentially the key's hedgehog (mortgage risk through the capital markets, profit per unit of risk, homeownership passion) and the same brutal facts, with Analysis 1 slightly closer on the stop-doing decision because it explicitly says to sell the fixed-rate book and move old-model executives off. Analysis 2 is sharper on the decline mechanism the key describes (backstop-fuelled portfolio growth, single-asset exposure to a national housing downturn, EPS-tied pay, restatements, government takeover), which makes it marginally the better document to hand to the leader.
